independence: Reviewer did not implement the canonical storage/log/fold repairs. The review directly read current source and fault-oracle assertions; it is separate from implementer re-reading, CI executions and PR bots.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: An uncertain root publication must remain distinguishable from a refused transaction, including after rollback failure.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: Journal frames use one actual end-of-file checkpoint. Root sync failure returns the original I/O refusal only after truncate/seek/sync rollback is confirmed; failed rollback poisons the handle. Public facade maps the exact poison code to ErrorKind::CommitOutcomeUnknown. Further writes refuse the poisoned handle.
findings_and_resolutions.oracle_review: Tests use the real per-store journal seam. Unknown-outcome test syncs the actual root, refuses rollback, checks scalar and vector errors, rejects a later write, closes, and independently reopens through Database to observe the landed operation.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: A vector pin-cleanup error could mask the journal poison code, or turn a committed write into an ordinary failure.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: vector_pin_cleanup_error structurally preserves chunk_store_journal_poisoned if either publication or release has that code. Known post-commit claimed-pin cleanup failure stays on the successful mutation path.
findings_and_resolutions.oracle_review: The maintenance test asserts the actual claimed-release seam was consumed, then closes and publicly reopens to resolve the committed vector. The unknown-outcome test includes the designated-vector path, exercising the outer error wrapper.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: A history/compaction test that only observes current vector search does not prove old vector payload survival.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: The oracle now resolves the historical vector payload via DiskObjectStore/read_vector_property and requires exact [1,0,0], both while pinned and after independent public reopen; the current vector is [0,1,0]. Exact old/new binary file payloads and catalog preservation are also asserted.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: A physically committed operation followed by fold-maintenance failure must not look uncommitted; stale materialization must not claim the log head is its graph watermark.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: FoldGraphStore commit_batch returns an Ok receipt with committed position and structured maintenance_failure after durable append. GraphWrite/GraphAtomic adapters report committed_fold_maintenance_failed with position rather than missing_write or silent success. Sticky maintenance/unknown states guard later mutations and checked views before early-return validation. pin_current reports graph.current_position. GraphVerify is not-ok for either failure state; independent reopen replays and clears the state.
findings_and_resolutions.oracle_review: Both pre-graph and post-graph/pre-algebra maintenance phases assert verify failure, truthful graph position, blocked later append, and successful independent recovery. Both ordinary and conditional trait adapters assert explicit known-committed errors.
findings_and_resolutions.limit: Existing infallible low-level GraphRead views can still expose the materialized snapshot after maintenance failure; checked views refuse, pin_current exposes its actual position, and maintenance_failure/verify disclose the condition. This review does not claim those infallible signatures became fallible.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: A partial physical append or lost sync acknowledgement could leave disk bytes while memory retained the old digest/position and accepted a misleading retry.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: PhysicalLog checkpoints actual length before length/payload/checksum/sync. Every fallible stage rolls back by truncate plus sync; only confirmed rollback returns the original refusal. Failed rollback retains typed candidate position/digest/cause, poisons append and verify, and ProposalCommitter checks poison before digest-idempotency lookup. Records/digest indexes publish only after successful append/sync.
findings_and_resolutions.oracle_review: FaultInjectingLogFile wraps actual NativeLogFile, writes partial bytes or syncs the actual file before returning the injected error, and tests truncate/rollback-sync refusal. Public PhysicalLog::open reconciles the same candidate digest; resumed append uses position2, and duplicate replay leaves bytes unchanged. This is real-file deterministic fault injection, not hardware power-loss proof.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: Extraction must retain the canonical LINKED_TO first-version writer boundary and product receipt/privacy enforcement.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: Generic stamp_first_version validates canonical tuple-derived identity, record schema, visibility object and first allocated/preserved version; InMemoryGraphStore::upsert_edge calls it after live endpoint checks and before publishing edge state. Theorem retains its product receipt/DATAWAVE validators and their real-consumer tests.
findings_and_resolutions.limit: Final06 downstream runtime acceptance is still building. This source review does not substitute for those tests or claim a full live permission audit.

findings_and_resolutions.finding: A portability oracle limited to node metadata or same-process reopen does not prove the full single-file database boundary.
findings_and_resolutions.resolution_reviewed: The parent closes the writer, copies only the .RR into a fresh directory containing one file, and launches a distinct child process. Child publicly opens read-only, queries records, resolves the directed edge/properties, checks vector ranking, resolves old/current node history, reads exact binary file bytes, and verifies. Parent asserts no added sidecar; child asserts the entire file bytes remain unchanged. A separate child cannot acquire an already-held writer.
findings_and_resolutions.limit: This receipt reviews the actual subprocess oracle implementation. Its execution result belongs to the separate native CI evidence, not this source review.

remaining_acceptance: Actual final Theorem native, embedded, prior-pack and product-ledger gates remain separate pending checks. Final worker WASM compilation has its own contract receipt. Storage CI results belong to the parent release evidence.
